sentence: Renault Group I Universal registration document 2024 Renault Group Sustainable development 2.2.2.6.1.2 Verification of compliance to DNSH criteria Climate change adaptation – all activities Following the TCFD approach, an assessment of climate risks and vulnerability, based on three scenarios: ● New Green Deal +1.5°C scenario; ● Eco-Techno Driven + 3°C scenario; ● Retreat and fragmentation +4°C scenario, was carried out to identify sites likely to be affected (See chapter 2.2.2.1.2) The identified physical climate risks have been assessed on the basis of the lifetime of the asset concerned and are essentially of three types (extreme heat, water stress and flooding) covered by appropriate action plans.
justification: Substantive use of TCFD approach: describes a specific climate risk and vulnerability assessment conducted under three named temperature scenarios (+1.5°C, +3°C, +4°C), identifying physical climate risks (extreme heat, water stress, flooding) across sites, showing concrete application of the TCFD framework.

sentence: Climate change mitigation – activity 5.4 related Direct emissions to heat production on remanufacturing sites are under 270 g CO2eq per kWh.

sentence: Transportation-related emissions are covered by Renault Group’s decarbonization initiative.

sentence: Sustainable use and protection of water and marine resources – all activities In addition to complying with applicable regulations and the ban on using any non-renewable water source, the factories are committed to reducing the quantities of water needed to produce a vehicle (See chapter 2.2.2.2.4) and to reducing toxic metal emissions that can impact water resources (See chapter 2.2.2.3.4).
justification: Factories are committed to reducing water quantities per vehicle and reducing toxic metal emissions impacting water resources — forward-looking commitments without specific numerical targets.

sentence: Transition to a circular economy – all activities except 2.6 and 5.4 Renault Group’s circular economy policy (See chapter 2.2.2.5) covers DNSH criteria related to (a) reuse and use of secondary raw materials and re-used components products manufactured, (b) design for high durability, recyclability, easy disassembly and adaptability of products manufactured, (c) waste management that prioritizes recycling over disposal in the manufacturing process, and (d) substances of concern which are identified and monitored throughout the life cycle (se chapter 2.2.2.2.2) Low-carbon vehicles involved in activity 6.5 are reusable or recyclable to a minimum of 85% by weight, reusable or recoverable to a minimum of 95% by weight, the Group complying with the European Directive 2000/53/EC on endof-life vehicles.
justification: Substantive use of EU Taxonomy DNSH criteria and European Directive 2000/53/EC: specifies concrete taxonomy-aligned thresholds (85% reusable/recyclable by weight, 95% reusable/recoverable) and maps circular economy policy to specific DNSH sub-criteria (a–d), demonstrating how the framework was applied.

justification: References multiple specific regulations (Delegated Regulation 2021/2139 Annex C, REACH Regulation 1907/2006, POPs, mercury regulations) with specific context of how Renault Group's substance policy meets criteria (a) to (e) and references a specific internal standard GDN-1903-2024-0002.
